head: From base model to reasoning flagship and distilled students
body: DeepSeek-R1 builds on DeepSeek-V3-Base through four post-training stages, followed by distillation into smaller open models. The process pairs reinforcement learning with rejection sampling to clean readability and eliminate language mixing.

First-stage RL encourages reasoning behaviors directly from cold-start seeds. Rejection sampling then harvests 800,000 verified trajectories for large-scale supervised fine-tuning, before a secondary RL stage tunes general helpfulness and safety.

head: GRPO trains reasoning without a separate critic network
body: Standard policy gradient methods such as PPO maintain a separate critic model of comparable size to compute baselines. This adds substantial GPU memory overhead and requires intermediate value predictions on long reasoning chains.

Group Relative Policy Optimization avoids the critic entirely. For each prompt, the old policy generates a group of outputs. Rule-based checks score each response, and advantage values are computed directly from the group mean and standard deviation.
The policy updates using a clipped objective regularised by KL divergence against a reference policy. This setup eliminates critic training overhead while supporting trajectories up to 65,536 tokens.
hint: Select any step to view how outputs are evaluated and updated.

nodes.label: Prompt
nodes.note: A batch contains 32 unique questions sampled during each rollout step.

nodes.label: Old Policy Rollout
nodes.note: The policy generates a group of G candidate outputs (G = 16 for DeepSeek-R1-Zero) for each prompt at temperature 1.

nodes.label: Accuracy check
nodes.note: Deterministic verification evaluates math box answers or runs code responses against unit test suites.

nodes.label: Format check
nodes.note: A reward checks whether the reasoning steps and final response are enclosed within explicit designated tags.

nodes.label: Rule-based rewards
nodes.note: Accuracy and format rewards are summed with equal weight. No neural reward model is used for reasoning tasks.

nodes.label: Group normalization
nodes.note: Advantages are calculated by normalizing each reward score against the mean and standard deviation of its group of G outputs. No critic network is needed.

nodes.label: Reference policy
nodes.note: The reference model provides an unbiased KL divergence penalty in the loss. It is refreshed with the latest policy every 400 steps.

nodes.label: Policy update
nodes.note: The policy optimizes the clipped surrogate objective with advantage A_i minus the KL penalty over 1 inner epoch.

head: Reinforcement learning expands thinking length and accuracy together
body: During pure reinforcement learning on DeepSeek-R1-Zero, the model learns to allocate more computation time to difficult questions without human demonstrations. Average response length expands from under 1,000 tokens to over 8,000 tokens as training proceeds.

Benchmark accuracy rises alongside output length. Pass@1 on AIME 2024 grows from 15.6% to 77.9%. Intermediate checkpoints develop reflective reasoning patterns, including spontaneous self-checking and backtracking.

states.text: Initial policy produces short chains of thought. Easy MATH problems are mastered early, but AIME accuracy starts low at 15.6%.
Thinking length grows. Frequency of reflective words rises 5- to 7-fold, and the model exhibits backtracking behaviors.
Reflective patterns stabilize. Extended test-time reasoning reaches 77.9% Pass@1 on AIME 2024, expanding up to 86.7% with consensus voting.

head: Cold-start SFT and preference tuning fix readability
body: DeepSeek-R1-Zero proves pure reinforcement learning can discover reasoning behaviors such as self-verification and backtracking directly from a base checkpoint. However, it suffers from severe language mixing and poor readability.

DeepSeek-R1 resolves these flaws by introducing a cold-start fine-tuning step, language consistency rewards, rejection sampling, and reward models for helpfulness and safety, while matching or slightly exceeding R1-Zero's benchmark performance.
hint: Select any row to view details on the implementation differences.

rows.label: Starting point
rows.note: R1-Zero trains directly on DeepSeek-V3-Base without any demonstration data. R1 begins with a small curated dataset of human-readable reasoning traces.

rows.label: Training pipeline
rows.note: R1-Zero relies exclusively on GRPO policy updates. R1 alternates between RL, rejection sampling SFT, and a secondary preference RL stage.

rows.label: Reward signals
rows.note: R1-Zero scores only accuracy and format. R1 combines rule-based rewards with a language consistency ratio and neural reward models for helpfulness and safety.

rows.label: Language mixing
rows.note: Because the base model is multilingual, R1-Zero frequently mixes languages during reasoning. R1 adds an explicit language consistency reward to penalize mixed tokens.

rows.label: Trace readability
rows.note: R1-Zero produces raw thought flows and only outputs the final answer in its summary. R1 refines the thinking process into a conversational style and provides detailed, readable solutions.

rows.label: AIME 2024 pass@1
rows.note: R1-Zero jumped from 15.6% to 77.9% during training. DeepSeek-R1 reaches 79.8% while providing human-aligned writing and format compliance.

head: Distillation from R1 outperforms direct RL on smaller base models
body: Applying pure reinforcement learning directly to a smaller base model induces reasoning, but supervised distillation from DeepSeek-R1 achieves substantially higher scores across every benchmark.
For Qwen-32B, distilling 800,000 reasoning traces beats 10,000 steps of direct RL by 25.6 percentage points on AIME 2024. For 7B models, distilled supervised fine-tuning similarly surpasses pure RL.
hint: Select a row to see model details and benchmark comparisons.

rows.label: 32B: AIME 2024 (pass@1)
rows.note: Qwen2.5-32B-Zero trained with direct RL for over 10K steps reaches 47.0%, while fine-tuning on R1 trajectories reaches 72.6%.

rows.label: 32B: MATH-500 (pass@1)
rows.note: Both approaches reach strong scores on MATH-500, but distillation retains an edge over direct RL without needing online exploration.

rows.label: 32B: GPQA Diamond
rows.note: Distillation transfers graduate-level scientific question-answering capabilities discovered by the larger 671B model during RL.

rows.label: 32B: LiveCodeBench
rows.note: Code synthesis shows a 17.0 percentage point gain with distillation over direct RL on the same 32B base model.

rows.label: 7B: AIME 2024 (pass@1)
rows.note: Direct RL on Qwen2-Math-7B reaches 22.3% on AIME 2024. In contrast, distilling R1 into Qwen2.5-Math-7B achieves 55.5%.

rows.label: Training recipe
rows.note: Direct RL requires heavy compute and reward verifiers. Distilled models rely strictly on supervised fine-tuning over 800,000 samples.

head: Around DeepSeek-R1 on the map
body: DeepSeek-R1 sits among the papers it builds on, reuses, measures itself against, and feeds. Colour shows how each relates; height shows how much DeepSeek-R1 leans on it. Hatched tiles are directions the paper leaves open.

tiles.label: DeepSeek-V3
tiles.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
tiles.link: DeepSeek-V3 provides the 671B mixture-of-experts base model that DeepSeek-R1 trains on. It also provides the general supervised dataset and the model used for judging and rewriting.
carried: Mixture-of-experts base architecture with 37B active parameters
Pre-training weights and multi-token prediction components
General instruction-following data pipeline
changed: Added rule-based reinforcement learning before supervised tuning
Added explicit chain-of-thought tags for intermediate reasoning
Trained for extended test-time thinking traces

tiles.label: GRPO
tiles.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
tiles.link: GRPO defines the reinforcement learning algorithm used across both training phases of DeepSeek-R1. It replaces the critic model in standard policy gradient methods with group-normalized scores.
carried: Group relative advantage estimation without a critic model
Clipped surrogate objective with reference policy divergence
Rule-based reward evaluation for verifiable math
changed: Scaled context length to 65,536 tokens during training
Added a language consistency reward component
Applied directly to a base model without prior SFT

tiles.label: PPO
tiles.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
tiles.link: PPO is the standard policy optimization algorithm in language model alignment. DeepSeek-R1 compares against it to demonstrate the memory and compute benefits of omitting the value model.
carried: Clipped probability ratio objective to constrain policy drift
Optimization using multiple rollout generations per prompt
changed: PPO trains a separate value network equal to policy size
PPO penalizes per-token KL divergence in the reward
GRPO computes advantage from group reward statistics

tiles.label: InstructGPT
tiles.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
tiles.link: InstructGPT established the standard post-training pipeline of supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning from human feedback. DeepSeek-R1 inverts this order for reasoning.
carried: Pairwise preference reward modeling for general queries
Post-training alignment for helpfulness and safety
changed: Eliminated supervised fine-tuning prior to initial RL
Replaced human preference rewards with rule checks for reasoning
Optimized for extended reasoning traces rather than concise text

tiles.label: Chain of Thought
tiles.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
tiles.link: Chain-of-thought prompting showed that generating intermediate tokens improves problem solving. DeepSeek-R1 automates the discovery of these intermediate trajectories via reinforcement learning.
carried: Step-by-step token generation preceding final answers
Inference-time compute scaling through intermediate tokens
changed: Eliminated few-shot human reasoning demonstrations
Autonomous emergence of self-reflection and verification
Scaling token chains up to tens of thousands of tokens

tiles.label: Process Supervision
tiles.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
tiles.link: Process reward models assign credit to each intermediate reasoning step. DeepSeek-R1 tested this approach but abandoned it because of reward hacking and step annotation difficulty.
carried: Intermediate reasoning verification improves problem accuracy
Mathematics problems provide measurable evaluation targets
changed: Process models evaluate every individual intermediate step
DeepSeek-R1 uses outcome-only rule checks on final answers
DeepSeek-R1 avoids training an intermediate neural verifier

tiles.label: AlphaGo / MCTS
tiles.title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search
tiles.link: Monte Carlo Tree Search guided by value networks achieved self-play improvements in board games. DeepSeek-R1 evaluated MCTS for token search but found the search space too large.
carried: Outcome feedback guides autonomous strategy improvement
Test-time compute search improves complex decision making
changed: MCTS searches discrete token branches with a value network
DeepSeek-R1 samples continuous reasoning chains directly
DeepSeek-R1 eliminates step-level value function estimation

tiles.label: STaR
tiles.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
tiles.link: STaR iteratively bootstraps reasoning by fine-tuning a model on its own successful solution paths. DeepSeek-R1 adopts a similar rejection sampling principle in its SFT phase.
carried: Filtering self-generated traces by final answer correctness
Supervised fine-tuning on correct reasoning trajectories
changed: Combines rejection sampling with full policy gradient RL
Applies rule verification on coding and STEM problems
Distills outputs into independent student model architectures

tiles.label: Model Distillation
tiles.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
tiles.link: Distillation transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. DeepSeek-R1 uses 800,000 teacher trajectories to train smaller Qwen and Llama checkpoints.
carried: Supervised training of student networks on teacher outputs
Preservation of reasoning capabilities in smaller architectures
changed: Distills explicit multi-step reasoning traces rather than logits
Applies supervised fine-tuning alone without student RL
Targets competitive mathematics and software tasks

tiles.label: QwQ-32B
tiles.title: QwQ: Reflect Deeply on the Boundaries of the Unknown
tiles.link: QwQ-32B is an open reasoning baseline. DeepSeek-R1 compares its distilled 32B model and pure RL 32B model directly against QwQ on reasoning benchmarks.
carried: Open release of long chain-of-thought model weights
Focus on competitive coding and mathematics benchmarks
changed: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B uses supervised distillation from 671B
DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B scores 72.6% on AIME 2024 versus 50.0%
DeepSeek documents the exact multi-stage training recipe

open.label: Tool-Integrated RL
open.title: Embedding external code execution and search directly into policy training
open.shows: DeepSeek-R1 operates without external tools, relying entirely on internal token generation for arithmetic, retrieval, and code validation.
open.open: The paper does not test whether adding tool calling actions into group policy optimization disrupts the emergence of internal self-reflection.
open.move: Add python interpreter tags into the GRPO action space on math tasks that exceed 64-bit integer precision and compare reasoning length.

open.label: Adaptive Token Budgets
open.title: Controlling token waste on simple tasks without degrading hard problem solving
open.shows: DeepSeek-R1 scales test-time compute dynamically with task complexity, but overthinks simpler questions like basic arithmetic.
open.open: It remains untested whether an explicit token budget reward penalty can curb verbosity on simple inputs without suppressing reflection on hard inputs.
open.move: Train a checkpoint with an added reward penalty proportional to generated tokens for inputs classified below a difficulty threshold.

open.label: Hybrid Verifier Signals
open.title: Combining outcome verification with formal automated intermediate checks
open.shows: Neural process reward models suffered from reward hacking, forcing the authors to rely exclusively on final outcome rewards.
open.open: Whether formal deterministic step checkers, such as interactive theorem prover steps, avoid the hacking observed in learned reward models.
open.move: Evaluate GRPO using formal Lean theorem proving environments where intermediate proof steps provide deterministic binary feedback.

open.label: Small Model Direct RL
open.title: Inducing long chain-of-thought behaviors directly in sub-10B base checkpoints
open.shows: Direct RL from scratch succeeded on 32B dense and 671B MoE base models, but failed on 7B dense and 16B MoE models due to repetitive loops.
open.open: The authors do not isolate whether failure in small models is caused by pre-training token volume, architecture width, or lack of reasoning traces.
open.move: Test GRPO on 7B models pre-trained with varying proportions of synthetic code-execution data to identify the threshold for RL emergence.
